title: fix(spec): the agent.tools liveness row says dead — it claimed live on a key the schema tombstoned
body:
Fixes #18304

Clause-②: no — a liveness row is a claim ABOUT the schema, not the schema. Judged against the actual diff below and it holds: no Zod schema, accept set or published export moves, and `check:authorable-surface` + `check:api-surface` both report their artifacts unchanged (see Readings). None of the 17 `packages/spec/api-surface-declarations/**` shards is in this diff.

## What was wrong

`packages/spec/liveness/agent.json`, prop `tools`:

```json
"tools": { "status": "live", "evidence": "cloud: packages/service-ai/src/agent-runtime.ts", "note": "legacy direct-tool fallback." }
```

The ledger README defines `live` as **"Has a runtime consumer"**. `agent.tools` was removed in protocol 17 (#3894) and `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts` declares it `retiredKey(...)`, which types the key `never` and rejects any authored value with the upgrade prescription. So the row certified a consumer for a key nothing can put a value into.

## The status was derived, not chosen

Two independent derivations, both re-measurable in this checkout:

**1. From the vocabulary.** The four published statuses are `live` / `experimental`–`planned` / `dead` / `live-elsewhere`.
- `live` — "Has a runtime consumer" — is refused: a `never`-typed key carries no value for anyone to consume, in any realm.
- `experimental` / `planned` — "Declared, intentionally not enforced yet" — is refused: the key is removed, not pending.
- `live-elsewhere` — "Dead here by measurement, **genuinely enforced in a sibling repo**" — is refused rather than left undeclared: it requires a real foreign enforcer, and a key nothing can carry a value for has nothing to enforce.
- `dead` — "Parsed, no consumer **anywhere the census looked**. Tracked for **enforce-or-remove** (ADR-0049)" — is the remaining reading, and it is the one that puts the key on the worklist it should have joined at protocol 17.

**2. From the ledger's own data.** Over the 36 governed types the gate walks, **40** top-level keys carry a `[REMOVED]` tombstone description and **all 40 are `never`-typed**. **39 of them already said `dead`.** `agent.tools` was the single outlier. The nearest precedents are in-class and in-type: `field.conditionalRequired` (#13043, `live` -> `dead`, row kept) and `agent.knowledge` in this very ledger.

The row **stays** rather than being deleted, which the README fixes as the rule for this route: "a `retiredKey()` tombstone **keeps** the key in the walked shape, so a tombstoned key's row must **stay**, while a strict-removed key's row must **go**."

## Which direction this moves the ledger

`live` -> `dead`, and **no key is added or removed**: the classified total stays at 1094, the accept set is byte-identical, and the type's own count moves `live 21 -> 20 / dead 1 -> 2`. Moving a verdict from `live` to `dead` makes the ledger **stricter** — it adds a row to the enforce-or-remove worklist and removes a false certification. No floor is lowered, no ratchet entry raised, no row deleted, no test skipped or quarantined.

## The cross-repo half is attributed, not re-asserted

Cloud is not reachable from an open-source checkout, and this seat did not reach it. The zero-consumer census in cloud `@cb8ee7ff` and its lit positive control (`agent.skills`, four real reads in the same tree) were taken by the #13272 re-verification on **2026-09-15**; that is the date `verifiedAt` carries and the row says whose reading it is. What replaces it as **load-bearing** is local and re-measurable: the `retiredKey` tombstone covers authored input, and the ADR-0087 conversion `agent-tools-to-skills` covers stored rows and built artifacts (the chain is replayed with retired entries included at every rehydration seam). Those two together mean no value reaches any consumer in any repo — a stronger claim than the cloud census, and one CI can hold.

## The second half the card raises: this row was EXEMPT from scrutiny

`scanEvidence` (`packages/spec/scripts/liveness/evidence.mts`) classifies a path-shaped token foreign when a realm marker is in force **or** when it starts with one of `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES`, and a foreign path is counted and never resolved. This row's citation was foreign in **both** of its spellings: `packages/services/service-ai/...` matched the prefix until #13309, and the explicit `cloud` marker that replaced it is attributed the same way. **What it implies:** the repoint in #13309 changed the row's exemption from implicit to declared, and changed nothing about its falsifiability — no gate could fail on it before or after, in either direction. Only a human, or a seat with cloud access, ever could. The stale `evidence` string is therefore deleted rather than repointed; a `dead` row's pointer lives in its `note` by the gate's own design (`EVIDENCE_UNSCANNED_STATUSES`).

Sibling rows hidden the same way are measured in Acceptance notes. ⛔ Nothing about `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES` is changed here — #13272's triage ruled that out and the ruling stands.

## Diff

| Path | Why |
|---|---|
| `packages/spec/liveness/agent.json` | the `tools` row: `live` -> `dead`, stale `evidence` deleted, `verifiedAt` + retirement story in `note`. Plus the ledger's own `_note`, whose sentence "the row keeps its `status` ... the liveness re-grade is triage's to make" **this change falsifies** — it now records the landed re-grade. Declared file-surface increment over the claim, which named the row alone. |
| `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts.md` | regenerated (`gen:liveness-counts`); never hand-patched |
| `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` | one clause in the hand-written `agent` Notes cell — the same half the `field.conditionalRequired` precedent (#13043) updated for its own re-grade |
| `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/tombstoned-row-status.test.ts` | new contract test against the real ledgers (below) |
| `.changeset/agent-tools-liveness-row-dead.md` | `patch` — measured below, `skip-changeset` is wrong |

## The test, and proof it can fail

A `[REMOVED]` tombstone's ledger row says `dead` — a class pin, not a datum echo, on a population of 40 with a non-vacuity floor. Nothing could catch the original defect: the forward pass and the orphan pass are both satisfied by a tombstone (it keeps the key in the walked shape), the evidence checks never ran on an attributed pointer, and `check-liveness.mts` reads `[experimental` / `[planned` markers with **no reading of `[REMOVED]` at all**.

Reverse verification, twice, from the committed state, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` so the mutation is proven on disk and the restore is proven against `HEAD`:

| Leg | Mutation (on-disk proof) | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `agent.tools` `dead` -> `live`; anchor 1 -> 0, replacement 10 -> 11, blob `77d2aa900129` -> `b6b8c9bf0cb0` | **RED**, 2 of 3 tests, naming `agent.tools → status=live` |
| 2 | `agent.knowledge` `dead` -> `live`; anchor 1 -> 0, replacement 0 -> 1, blob `77d2aa900129` -> `024d4df25361` | **RED**, 1 of 3, naming `agent.knowledge → status=live` — so the pin is a CLASS pin; the `agent.tools` case stayed green |

Both legs restored with `blob == HEAD (77d2aa900129)` and `git diff HEAD` empty. Direction predicted before running: turns red. Direction observed: turns red. No dist mediates either leg — the test imports `src/` and reads the ledger JSON from disk — so no `dist` preflight applies, and the on-disk proof is the whole chain. No permanent ablation artefact is left behind.

## Readings — instrument, unit, control

All taken in this worktree at `447f4f21b`, cut from `origin/main` at `abb01f105`.

| Reading | Instrument | Value | Lit control |
|---|---|---|---|
| tombstoned keys whose row is not `dead` | walk the 36 governed types for a `[REMOVED]` description, join the ledger status | **1** before (`agent.tools`), **0** after | 40 tombstones found, all `never`-typed, 39 already `dead` — the detector fires |
| `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES` still matched by any evidence field | `scanEvidence` over all 39 ledgers | **0** fields | **26** fields cite the real `packages/service-ai/` path |
| scanned-status rows whose evidence resolves to zero local paths (no gate can fail on them) | `scanEvidence`, 39 ledgers, 481 rows | **61** rows | **254** rows carry at least one local path the gate CAN fail on |
| unresolvable foreign pointers in the gate's own census | `check:liveness` summary line | **212 -> 211**; local resolvable **583 -> 583** | the local count is the control: this change adds no pointer CI must resolve |
| `verifiedAt` coverage | `check:liveness` summary line | dated **628 -> 629**, undated **235 -> 234**, 0 older than 180d | — |
| does the ledger actually publish? | `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` in `packages/spec` (`liveness` is in `files[]`) | `liveness/agent.json`, `liveness/state-counts.md`, `liveness/README.md` all **shipped** (292 files) | the new test file is **not** shipped, and **no** `scripts/` path is — the packer discriminates |

Changeset judgement: published content moves ⇒ a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong. `patch`, on the `7cd587413` precedent (a one-line `liveness/field.json` note repoint took a `patch`).

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (65 commands, derived from the merge base rather than a hand-written diff).

- **62 of the 65 green**, exit code captured before any pipe in every case.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — **all 16 generated artifacts up to date**, including `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface` and `check:liveness` (the counts file current). This is the mechanical half of the `Clause-②: no` judgement.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` green. The new test file is compiled by `tsconfig.scripts.json` — measured with `tsc --listFiles` (1 hit there, 0 in `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.test.json`), so `check:scripts-typecheck` really covers it.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local` — **492 files, 14298 tests, 0 failures**.
- **NOT MEASURED (3), each exiting 3 = `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, declared to CI rather than read as green:** `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt`. All three read built output across the whole workspace and this diff touches no package source; a whole-repo build is CI's.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run, not narrowed here.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, noted rather than filed from here:

1. **The liveness gate has no reading of `[REMOVED]`.** `check-liveness.mts`'s `markerStatus()` knows `[experimental` and `[planned` only, so a tombstoned key may carry any status and no gate objects — the mechanism that let this row sit `live` for three months. The class invariant is pinned by a test in this PR, but the gate itself still cannot see a tombstone. A gate leg would start green at 40/40 after this lands. Dedupe words: `liveness tombstone status`, `retiredKey ledger dead`, `markerStatus REMOVED`.
2. **61 rows are unfalsifiable by construction** (measured above, control 254). The card names this asymmetry for `agent.tools`; the population is the general case, and `agent.tools` was its sharpest instance because the outlier was also tombstoned locally. After this change **no** tombstoned row carries a non-`dead` status, so the sharpest class is empty — the remaining 60 are ordinary cross-repo claims resting on dated readings. ⛔ Not fixed here.
3. `FOREIGN_PATH_PREFIXES` matches zero evidence fields across all 39 ledgers (control: 26 cite the real path), i.e. the constant is inert. Already recorded on the card, which rules out touching it.
4. **Next step is a separate card:** with the row `dead`, `agent.tools` is an ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove input (playbook `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement`). Triage was explicit that the retirement is not this card's.
